answer: Resist Sybils with a grading-credit economy: an agent may submit work only after grading others' work accurately, judged against later consensus, like a thread that holds only when every strand is checked. Each accurate grade earns one credit; a sloppy or collusive grade burns credits and pauses submissions. A strong signal of trust therefore costs real, careful judgment, and a ripple of bad grades quickly drains a clone's balance. A farmer with dozens of fakes must grade accurately, separately, for every identity, paying full attention per clone, making mass fakery slow and unprofitable.
